channel.title: NPR Programs: Morning Edition
channel.description: Morning Edition takes listeners around the country and the world with multi-faceted stories and commentaries every weekday. Hosts Steve Inskeep, Leila Fadel, Michel Martin and A Martínez bring you the latest breaking news and features to prepare you for the day.

item.title: Democrats have a long to-do list when they take over Congress next year
item.description: Democrats ran on lowering costs and stamping out corruption before securing control of Congress Tuesday. But how will they accomplish their goals amid tension with President Trump?
item.content:encoded: Democrats ran on lowering costs and stamping out corruption before securing control of Congress Tuesday. But how will they accomplish their goals amid tension with President Trump?
item.dc:creator: Sam Gringlas

item.title: Sen. Gillibrand says Democrats must end Iran war, hold Trump accountable. But how?
item.description: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand spoke with Morning Edition about Democrats' priorities, from lowering costs to ending the Iran war. But questions remain about how they'll deliver.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Mike Johnson says he will step aside as top House Republican next Congress
item.description: Speaker Mike Johnson won't stay on as GOP leader in the House when the new Congress convenes in January. His decision follows crushing losses by Republicans in the midterm election.
item.content:encoded: Speaker Mike Johnson won't stay on as GOP leader in the House when the new Congress convenes in January. His decision follows crushing losses by Republicans in the midterm election.
item.dc:creator: Claudia Grisales

item.title: Democrats will control Congress. Will it change Trump's approach to foreign policy?
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with historian and journalist Anne Applebaum about how much a Democrat-led Congress can steer foreign policy.
item.content:encoded: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with historian and journalist Anne Applebaum about how much a Democrat-led Congress can steer foreign policy.

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: Democrats are planning out how to tackle their agenda in the new year, ballots are still being counted in some undecided races, Trump avoids taking the blame after GOP midterm losses.

item.title: Alanis Morissette blends music and storytelling for her new concert series
item.description: NPR's A Martinez visits 90s music icon Alanis Morissette as she prepares for her residency "Butterfly with a Machete," a series of concerts in Los Angeles that are part musical performance, part storytelling.

item.title: Democrats will take control of Congress next year. What does it mean for the economy?
item.description: The Democratic gains in this week's midterm elections will bring a different business climate to Washington. But the overall economy should be OK.

item.title: Cuba grapples with ongoing economic and energy crisis
item.description: Cuba continues to grapple with a deepening economic and energy crisis, as widespread power outages, fuel shortages and rising tensions with the U.S. add to uncertainty across the island.

item.title: A look at how the NYPD built its surveillance system and the fight for transparency
item.description: New York City police surveillance systems were paid for and adopted without the kind of public oversight cities usually require.

item.title: Iran wary of new U.S. attacks despite Trump noting war's role in election losses
item.description: Both President Trump and Vice President JD Vance acknowledged the role the Iran war played in the GOP's election loss. Iran agrees, but it is wary of new attacks.
